rig: Fanatec GT DD Pro (5 Nm, Boost Kit 180 pending) + bundled Steering Wheel for Gran Turismo DD Pro + CSL Pedals (Load Cell Kit pending), PS5

evidence_labels.V: official Fanatec/EA/Polyphony source (text, figure, help article, product page, Fanatec video caption)
evidence_labels.A: seen in Fanatec's own low-resolution (320x180) video frames
evidence_labels.U: owner report, community guide, or not confirmed

display.name: White OLED display on the steering wheel
display.where: Top centre of the steering wheel, directly above the round GT logo and just below the curved RevLED light strip. The wheel base has no display.
display.shows: Profile item: one word such as AUTO, C SET or SET 4 [A]. A setting: the value in big digits, a small label in the top corner (probably the item name), and a bar under numeric values [A]. 'CAL' when centre calibration is needed. Fanatec text: 'A.SET.' when a game actively uses Auto Setup (OLED appearance [U]). With the menu closed it may be blank or show game data ('telemetry output (where supported)', PROD).
display.size: not confirmed (a search summary claimed 1-inch 128x64; no Fanatec page found saying so)
display.source: PROD; M p17, p19, p20; VID25 frames 10:20-11:45
display.verifier_note: added RevLED locator, what the OLED shows (from fresh video frames) and closed-menu behaviour

tuning_button.name: Tuning Menu button
tuning_button.where: Tiny round button immediately LEFT of the display, between the display and the 'L2' tab; much smaller than the other buttons.
tuning_button.label: not confirmed: no source shows a legible label on the button. Fanatec drawings use a three-sliders icon for 'Enter/Exit Tuning Menu' (manual p17, QG), not shown to be printed on the rim.
tuning_button.hold_3_to_4_s_with_menu_open: toggle Standard <-> Advanced menu (Fanatec gives 3 s in FAQ36/VID25/D431 and 4 s in M p21/H-ADV)
tuning_button.hold_about_6_s_more: RESET of all custom setups to factory values; returns to Standard menu. M p21/H-ADV say 'additional 6 seconds'; one EXP caption reads like 6 s in total. Never hold past 5 s.
tuning_button.source: M p19 figure, p21; QG panels G/H; GTP22; VID25 10:20, 11:00, 11:45; FAQ36; D431

menu_stick.name: Menu stick (manual: 'D-Pad'; Fanatec 2025 video: 'D-Stick'; product page: '5-way directional stick for menu navigation')
menu_stick.where: Lower LEFT of the wheel face, below the blue-ringed stick. Not one of the four coloured-ring sticks.
menu_stick.left_right: move between settings (items); which direction is 'next' is not confirmed
menu_stick.up_down: change the value; on the first item (profile) choose the profile; in A SET only shows the game's value
menu_stick.which_way_is_next_or_increase: not confirmed; GTPlanet 2022 implies UP steps from AUTO to SET 1 to SET 2
menu_stick.confirm_button: none: changes are used and saved immediately
menu_stick.source: M p19 figure; PROD; FAQ36 ('directional stick'); VID25 captions 10:20-11:40; GTP22
menu_stick.verifier_note: left/right direction semantics downgraded to unconfirmed

coloured_ring_sticks.name: Four additional 5-way directional sticks (green, blue left; red, yellow right)
coloured_ring_sticks.use: game inputs; NOT used for the Tuning Menu
coloured_ring_sticks.colours_evidence: A (video frames only; PROD names no colours)
coloured_ring_sticks.verifier_note: ring colours are A, not V

face_buttons.layout: lower right cluster: triangle top, square left, circle right, cross bottom

hub_top_small_buttons.left: small round button under the L2 tab (icon resembles PlayStation CREATE; name not confirmed)
hub_top_small_buttons.right: small round button under the R2 tab with a three-line symbol (resembles PlayStation OPTIONS; name not confirmed)
hub_top_small_buttons.mode_change_combo: left small button + triangle (manual p16 figure, highlighted positions)
hub_top_small_buttons.centre_calibration_combo: right small button + cross (manual p17 figure, highlighted positions)
hub_top_small_buttons.source: M p16, p17 figures; VID25 frames
hub_top_small_buttons.note: positions of both combos are V (M p16/p17, EXP I/K, QG F/G figures); button names and icons are A

power_button.where: Right-hand side of the wheel base, towards the front (wheel end) [A], power symbol; its ring LED shows the mode colour
power_button.press_1_s: power on (base runs start-up calibration; hands off the wheel)
power_button.source: M p15, p16, p29; EXP H; QG panels E, I; VID25 06:15-06:40

mode_led.DARK BLUE: PlayStation native: use for PS5 (F1 25, GT7)
mode_led.PURPLE: PS4 compatibility: detected as CSL Elite Wheel Base+ PS4; only for old games (e.g. F1 2020)
mode_led.RED: PC native; needed for firmware updates
mode_led.YELLOW: PC compatibility: detected as ClubSport Wheel Base V2.5
mode_led.persistence: mode is kept across power cycles except after a firmware update
mode_led.cycle_order: not confirmed; VID25 shows blue, red, purple, yellow in that order [A]
mode_led.source: M p16; H-MODES; H-BLUE; EXP I; VID25
mode_led.GREEN: Xbox; needs an Xbox wheel, so not seen with the bundled GT wheel (H-MODES)
mode_led.verifier_note: video colour order and green note added

ports.usb: supplied 'USB Type-A to Type-C' cable; USB-A end to the PS5 [D]
ports.power_order: DC plug into the base before the AC plug into the wall

steps.text: Find the screen: the small white window at the top centre of the steering wheel, above the GT logo and just below the curved light strip. The base has no screen.
steps.check: It shows menu text when you short-press the Tuning button (with the menu closed it may be blank or show game data).

steps.text: Find the Tuning Menu button: the tiny round button just LEFT of the screen.
steps.check: One short press turns the screen on with a menu item.

steps.text: Find the menu stick: the stick at the lower LEFT of the wheel face, under the blue-ringed stick. Ignore the four coloured-ring sticks.
steps.check: With the menu open, tilting it right changes the item name on the screen.

steps.text: Remember the directions: LEFT/RIGHT = move between settings; UP/DOWN = change the value (on the first item: change profile). Which of LEFT/RIGHT is 'next' is not confirmed; if you go the wrong way, tilt the other way.
steps.check: The small label changes with left/right; the big number changes with up/down.

steps.text: Find the power button on the right-hand side of the wheel base; its ring shows the mode colour.
steps.check: Ring is lit after power-on.

steps.text: Learn the screen: on a setting, the big digits are the value, the small text in the top corner is which setting you are on, and numbers have a bar underneath.
steps.check: Big number changes when you tilt up/down.

walkthroughs.title: Power on and set PlayStation (dark blue) mode

steps.text: Put the steering wheel on the base. QR2 Lite: press it firmly onto the base's quick release (the top of the base-side part is more rounded, so it fits one way only). To remove: pull the sleeve on the wheel side while pulling the wheel towards you.
steps.check: The wheel does not wobble or come off when pulled gently.
steps.note: Older bundles have QR1 Lite (M p4); then follow M p10. Which version this rig has is unknown [U].

steps.text: Before power-on plug in: the pedal RJ12 cable from the throttle module port 'Wheel Base / Load Cell' to the base port 'Pedals'; the power brick into the base first, then into the wall; the supplied USB cable to the PS5.
steps.check: Cables seated; devices are detected after start-up.
steps.source: M p1, p2, p5, p6 (4.1 ATTENTION), p11, p13
steps.verifier_note: port names and power-brick order added

steps.text: Press the power button for about 1 second. Keep your hands off the wheel while it moves during start-up calibration.
steps.check: Ring lights up; the wheel moves briefly and settles.

steps.text: Wait until start-up has finished before changing mode.
steps.check: Wheel has stopped moving.

steps.text: Read the ring colour: dark blue = PlayStation (PS5). Purple = PS4 compatibility, red = PC, yellow = PC compatibility.
steps.check: Ring is dark blue.
steps.source: M p16 (5.3); EXP I; H-MODES; H-BLUE; VID25 06:15-06:35

steps.text: If not dark blue: tap (short press, under 1 s) the power button once, wait for the colour to change, repeat until dark blue. Never hold it (3 s turns the base off).
steps.check: Ring is dark blue.
steps.note: Tap order not confirmed; the video shows blue, red, purple, yellow in that order [A].

steps.text: Alternative wheel combination (not needed): small round button under the L2 tab together with triangle.
steps.check: Ring colour changes.
steps.note: The combination exists (V: M p16, EXP I, QG F); the buttons are identified from figure positions (A).

steps.text: The mode is remembered after power off/on, except after a firmware update: check the colour after updates.
steps.check: Ring still dark blue after next power-on.

walkthroughs.title: Open the Tuning Menu, move, change a value, close

steps.text: Short-press the Tuning button. In Fanatec's video the menu opens on the profile item (AUTO / C SET / SET n). If you see a number instead, tilt LEFT or RIGHT until a profile name appears.
steps.check: A profile name is on the screen.
steps.source: VID25 frame 10:30 [A]; profile names in text: M p20-21, FAQ36; OLED spelling: VID25 frames, GTP22
steps.verifier_note: was verified=true; no Fanatec text says the menu always opens on the profile item

steps.text: Tilt the menu stick LEFT or RIGHT to move to another setting. If you go the wrong way, tilt the other way.
steps.check: The small label and the value change.
steps.source: VID25 11:25-11:40 ('Left and right switches between the available settings')
steps.verifier_note: 'RIGHT = next' was presented as verified; direction is U

steps.text: Tilt UP or DOWN to change the value.
steps.check: The big number changes and the bar under it grows or shrinks [A].
steps.source: VID25 ('Up and down adjusts the values'); FAQ36

steps.text: There is no confirm button: the value is used and saved at once in the base.
steps.check: Close and re-open the menu: the value is still there.

steps.text: Short-press the Tuning button again to close the menu.
steps.check: Menu text disappears from the screen.
steps.source: VID25 11:45; QG panel H step 3; EXP M step 3

steps.text: The menu works at any time, even while a game is running. Use it while stopped or paused.
steps.source: EXP-TM ('accessed at any time ... even on consoles')

walkthroughs.title: Standard vs Advanced: tell, switch, and avoid the reset

steps.text: To tell which menu you are in: on the profile item tilt UP/DOWN. Standard offers only Auto and Custom (A SET / C SET; on the OLED AUTO / C SET [A]); Advanced offers Auto plus 1 SET..5 SET (on the OLED SET 1..SET 5 [A]). Any profile with a number = Advanced.
steps.check: You see 1 SET..5 SET = Advanced.
steps.verifier_note: OLED spellings and simplest test added

steps.text: Or tilt LEFT/RIGHT through the items: Standard shows only SEN, FF, NDP (+BRF with a load-cell brake; SHO/MPS only with supporting hardware). Advanced adds FFS, NFR, NIN, INT, FEI, FOR, SPR, DPR. FUL (FullForce) exists on GT DD Pro firmware since June 2026, but which menu shows it is [U].
steps.check: INT or FEI visible = Advanced.
steps.source: M p21-25; EXP M; VID25 ('three core parameters'); PROD; H-TORQUE; FF-BLOG
steps.verifier_note: FUL existence now V; menu location U

steps.text: Extra clue: in Standard NDP stops at 25 and FF at 005; in Advanced both go to OFF.
steps.check: NDP can reach OFF = Advanced.

steps.text: Before your first switch, write your slot values down (pitwall Setup tab) so an accidental reset only costs re-typing.
steps.check: Values recorded.
steps.source: derived from M p21 reset behaviour

steps.text: To switch: short-press the Tuning button so the menu is open, then press and HOLD it, counting 'one-thousand-one...'. Fanatec says 3 s (FAQ, video, driver notes) or 4 s (manual, help).
steps.check: The screen changes while you hold (GTPlanet 2022: 'MOD CHANGED TO ADVANCED' [U]); the profile item now offers SET 1..SET 5 (Advanced) or only AUTO / C SET (Standard).
steps.source: FAQ36; VID25 11:00; D431; M p21; H-ADV; EXP M; GTP22

steps.text: Let go as soon as the screen changes and never hold past 5 s. If nothing happened, let go and try again. Holding on resets ALL custom profiles to factory values and returns to Standard: the manual says after an additional 6 s (~10 s total), but one Fanatec caption reads like 6 s in total.
steps.check: Your 1 SET values are still there afterwards.
steps.verifier_note: reset timing ambiguity; limit changed from '~10 s' framing to 'never past 5 s'

steps.text: The same hold toggles back to Standard. Whether slot values survive a normal toggle (without the long reset), and which profile is active afterwards, are not documented.
steps.check: Re-check a slot value after toggling.

walkthroughs.title: Choose a custom slot (1 SET..5 SET)

steps.text: Be in the Advanced menu.
steps.check: 1 SET..5 SET are offered on the first item.

steps.text: Go to the profile item; tilt UP/DOWN until it shows 1 SET (on the OLED most likely 'SET 1' [A]). Suggested: 1 SET = F1 25, 2 SET = GT7 custom, 3 SET = experiments.
steps.check: Slot name on the screen.
steps.source: VID25 11:20 ('Up and down switches between different setup profiles'); RSS 6.0

steps.text: Selecting the profile activates it; close the menu with it showing.
steps.check: Re-open the menu: the first item still shows your slot.
steps.source: FAQ36 ('Select the Custom setup to activate it')

steps.text: A SET = Auto Setup: the game controls the values; you can view but not change them (trying to change one shows the game's value). It is the factory default. Fanatec's text says the screen shows 'A.SET.' when a game actively uses it; how that looks on this OLED is [U]. Owners describe the settings as 'locked'; the exact on-screen word is not confirmed.
steps.check: If values refuse to change you are in A SET: pick 1 SET (or C SET in Standard).
steps.verifier_note: 'A.SET.' appearance on this OLED downgraded to U

steps.text: If no game sends values, A SET simply uses the factory defaults (SEN AUTO, FF 100, NDP 50 ...).
Switching to Advanced may leave you on A SET (one owner: more items appeared but stayed 'locked'). Always pick SET 1 after switching.
steps.check: Profile item shows SET 1, and values change.

steps.text: Changes save immediately; each slot keeps its own values in the base across power cycles.
steps.check: Power-cycle the base, re-open the menu, read a value back.

walkthroughs.title: Change each value in your slot

steps.text: Select your slot, tilt RIGHT (or LEFT) once, read the small label, tilt UP/DOWN until the big number shows the target, move to the next item; repeat for every item on your sheet.
steps.check: Each item shows your target number.
steps.verifier_note: label is small on the OLED; direction not confirmed

steps.text: To choose OFF: the manual lists OFF just before the lowest number ('OFF 001 ... 100'), so it is probably one step below the lowest number. For BLI the manual lists OFF after 100.
steps.check: Screen shows OFF.
steps.verifier_note: was V; position of OFF is inferred from list order

steps.text: SEN starts at AUTO. The manual lists AUTO after the highest number ('90 ... 2520 AUTO'), so one step from AUTO probably lands on 2520 (Advanced) or 1080 (Standard); then step down to 360. If you land on 90, go the other way.
steps.check: Screen shows 360.
steps.source: M p22 list order; VID25 frame 11:25 shows 2520 [A]

steps.text: Close the menu, re-open it and re-read two items.
steps.check: They still show your values.

steps.text: SEN check: with SEN 360 the base stops the wheel at about half a turn (180 deg) each way from centre (manual: SEN 90 allows 45 deg each way).
steps.check: Wheel stops near 180 deg each side.

steps.text: The order of items in the menu is not confirmed (manual describes SEN, FF, FFS, NDP, NFR, NIN, INT, FEI, FOR/SPR/DPR, BLI, SHO, MPS, AP, BRF).
steps.check: Read each item name before changing it.

walkthroughs.title: CSL Pedals (stock Hall sensors): routine after every power-on

steps.text: Plug the pedals (RJ12) into the base before power-on.
steps.check: Pedals respond in game.

steps.text: After every power-on, before driving: press the throttle all the way down and let it all the way back; press the brake as far as it goes and let it all the way back (clutch too if fitted).
steps.check: pitwall Live tab (F1 25 telemetry on, on track): brake and throttle bars read 0 at rest and 100 at full press.

steps.text: Stock CSL Pedals have no BRF setting.
steps.check: BRF does not appear in the menu.
steps.source: M p28 ('Not supported by the included CSL Pedals')

walkthroughs.title: After the CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit: find and set BRF

steps.text: Update the base firmware first: Windows PC with the Fanatec App, base in RED, then return to DARK BLUE. A Mac cannot do this. Expect 'CAL' afterwards (centre calibration) and re-check the mode colour.
steps.check: Ring dark blue again.

steps.text: Wire per the LC manual: short RJ12 from the accelerator 'Wheel Base / Load Cell' port to the load-cell module 'Load Cell' port; load-cell module to the wheel base with the long RJ12 from the CSL Pedals; old brake may go to 'Clutch'. Never connect RJ12 and USB at the same time. Check the printed port labels.
steps.check: Ports match the printed labels.

steps.text: Power on and press every pedal fully and release (needed when Manual Mode is not set, i.e. always on PS5 without a PC).
steps.check: Brake bar 0 at rest, 100 at a firm press.
steps.note: That Manual Mode is never set on a PS5-only rig is D: it can only be enabled from PC software (LCK 4.5).

steps.text: Open the menu, choose your slot, tilt LEFT/RIGHT until BRF appears. It shows in Standard and Advanced, but only when the load-cell brake is detected.
steps.check: BRF is listed; if not, check wiring and firmware.

steps.text: Set BRF with UP/DOWN: Lo, 010..100, Hi; default 050. Lower = less force for 100% brake.
steps.check: pitwall Live brake bar reaches 100 at your chosen firm press.

steps.text: Re-check BRF after base restarts and firmware updates (past BRF-reset bugs).
steps.check: BRF still shows your value.

steps.text: Manual p28, EXP M (BRF), H-TM and LCK 4.5 all say BRF needs RJ12 'and' USB; LCK 4.4 says never both; EXP M's Standard-menu note only requires a load-cell pedal set, and LCK 4.5 says BRF is also in the Tuning Menu. On PS5 use RJ12 only. Whether BRF is per slot or global is not confirmed.
steps.check: BRF visible with RJ12 only.
steps.source: M p28; EXP M; H-TM; LCK 4.4, 4.5
steps.verifier_note: the 'RJ12 and USB' wording is not only in the PDF

walkthroughs.title: F1 25 on PS5: where the in-game settings are

steps.text: Main menu or pause menu: Settings > Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback.
steps.check: You see a list of input devices/presets.
steps.source: BK25 (2025-05-28, 'Settings > Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel] > Calibration'); SRS25; EA-F122 controls (F1 22)

steps.text: Select your wheel's entry (not the Wireless Controller). The exact name F1 25 shows for the GT DD Pro is not confirmed.
steps.check: Wheel entry opens with Calibration and Vibration & Force Feedback options.
steps.note: EA's F1 22 page calls these entries 'Wireless Controller Preset 1/2'.

steps.text: Calibration: Steering/Throttle/Brake Deadzone, Linearity, Saturation (0-100, default 0 in EA's F1 22 docs). F1 25 also has 'Steering Rate' per BK25.
steps.check: Sliders show your values.
steps.verifier_note: Steering Rate is not in EA's F1 22 list

steps.text: Vibration & Force Feedback (BK25: 'Vibration & Feedback'). F1 25 per BK25: Vibration & Force Feedback On/Off, Strength, On Track Effects, Rumble Strip Effects, Off Track Effects, Pit Stop Effects, Wheel Damper, Maximum Wheel Rotation. EA's F1 22 list instead has Understeer Enhance and two rotation items (F1 & F2 default 360; Super Cars default 900) and no Pit Stop Effects. If there are two rotation items, set the F1 one.
steps.check: All items listed.
steps.verifier_note: Pit Stop Effects was credited to EA F1 22; it is BK25-only

steps.text: Set Maximum Wheel Rotation to the same number as SEN on the wheel (e.g. 360 and 360).
steps.check: Turn the real wheel to 90 deg: the in-game wheel is at 90 deg too. If not, Fanatec's fix is to change SEN until they match; some games' wheel animation is not realistic.

steps.text: Set SEN by hand for F1; do not rely on SEN AUTO (Fanatec known issue; observed on PC, PS5 behaviour unknown).
steps.check: SEN shows a number, not AUTO.

steps.text: If items seem missing, look for a settings filter and set it to Expert.
steps.check: Calibration and effect sliders visible.
steps.source: RSS 3.5 (not confirmed in an EA source)

walkthroughs.title: GT7 on PS5: Force Feedback Max. Torque and Sensitivity

steps.text: Before a race, in the Quick Menu choose Settings > Controller Settings.
steps.check: Controller Settings screen opens.

steps.text: Under Steering Force Feedback set 'Force Feedback Max. Torque' and 'Force Feedback Sensitivity'. The official manual gives no ranges (owners use 1-10).
steps.check: Values shown.

steps.text: On the wheel GT7 can use A SET (game-pushed, read-only) or your own slot (e.g. 2 SET).
steps.check: Profile item shows A SET or 2 SET.
steps.source: M p20 (Auto Setup in general); RSS 2 and 6.4 (GT7 1.71 notice: GT7 uses A SET)
steps.verifier_note: GT7's use of A SET is not in the manual

steps.text: Whether Controller Settings is also reachable while paused is not confirmed.

Known GT DD Pro issues in GT7: FFB can be lost with the wheel spinning uncontrollably; SPR and DPR do not work in the GT7 menu. If the wheel spins on its own: hands off, hold power 3 s to switch the base off.
steps.check: Base off; wheel stops.

walkthroughs.title: Centre calibration ('CAL' flashing or wheel off-centre)

steps.text: 'CAL' flashing on the wheel screen is normal after a base firmware update.
steps.check: 'CAL' visible.

steps.text: Short-press the Tuning button to open the menu.
steps.check: Menu open.
steps.source: M p17 step 1; QG panel G; VID25 08:40-08:45

steps.text: Hold the wheel dead straight.
steps.check: Wheel centred.

steps.text: Press together: the small round button under the R2 tab (top-right of the hub, three-line symbol) and cross (bottom face button).
steps.check: 'CAL' disappears.
steps.source: M p17 step 3 figure; EXP K; QG panel G (positions); VID25 08:50-08:55 (names)
steps.note: Positions are V (three Fanatec figures); the names cross and three-line symbol are A.
steps.verifier_note: positions are verified by official figures; only the button names are A

steps.text: Short-press the Tuning button to exit. If the wheel still won't centre, make sure SPR is not low or OFF.
steps.check: Wheel returns to centre after start-up.
steps.source: M p17 step 4; M p25; VID25 ~08:55

SETUP.display: Fanatec text: A SET / C SET (Standard); A SET / 1 SET..5 SET (Advanced). OLED in VID25: AUTO, C SET, SET 4 [A]. 'A.SET.' when a game actively uses Auto Setup (text; OLED look [U])
SETUP.default: A SET (Auto Setup is the factory default)

SEN.values: degrees: Standard 180..1080 or AUTO; Advanced 90..2520 or AUTO; step size not confirmed
SEN.note: set by hand for F1 and match Maximum Wheel Rotation. AUTO is listed after the highest value, so from AUTO you probably step down from 2520/1080 [D]

FF.display: FF (Fanatec web pages and PC App: FFB)

FFS.values: LIN / PEA (App and Fanatec pages: LINEAR / PEAK)
FFS.note: RSS 3.1: not offered with the Boost Kit on base FW >= 1.9.0.2; conflicts with help 50420340753297 (2026-09-24) which still says set PEAK for 8 Nm. If shown, set PEA.
FFS.verifier_note: conflict with a September 2026 help article added

FEI.values: 000..100 (000 smoothest, 100 sharpest); steps of 10 on older bases per FAQ36, not confirmed for GT DD Pro

SPR.values: OFF, 010..120; low/OFF stops the base re-centring the wheel after centre calibration

BRF.values: Lo, 010..100, Hi (Lo = least force for 100% brake); only when a load-cell brake is detected
BRF.source: M p21, p28; EXP M; LCK 4.5

FUL.values: OFF..100 per H-TM (written for Podium/CS DD) [U for GT DD Pro]
FUL.note: FullForce is on the GT DD Pro from the June 2026 firmware (V: PROD note, H-TORQUE, FF-BLOG). H-TM still says 'ONLY for Podium DD, CS DD and CS DD+' (out of date). Known issue: weaker than intended (APP1613). Leave at default for F1.
FUL.source: PROD; H-TORQUE; FF-BLOG; H-TM; APP1613; RSS 3.1
FUL.verifier_note: existence upgraded to V; menu, position and range on GT DD Pro remain U

display_format_note.display: manual writes leading zeros (050, 001, 010; 01 for NDP/INT)
display_format_note.values: OLED shows the value in big digits, a small label in the top corner and a bar under numbers [A]; leading zeros, % / deg signs, FF-vs-FFB spelling and whether the label is text or an icon not confirmed

mistakes.cause: Profile is A SET (Auto Setup, 'AUTO' on the OLED), the factory default
mistakes.fix: First item: choose C SET (Standard) or 1 SET (Advanced), then change values

mistakes.symptom: Even custom profiles cannot be changed; menu seems frozen
mistakes.cause: Firmware fault (Fanatec article 'Tuning Menu is locked'); the article gives no symptom detail, so rule out A SET first
mistakes.fix: Re-flash base firmware from a Windows PC with the Fanatec App (base in RED), then back to DARK BLUE
mistakes.verifier_note: rule out A SET first; Windows-only

mistakes.symptom: INT, FEI, FOR, FFS etc. missing; NDP won't go below 25
mistakes.fix: Open menu, hold Tuning button 3-4 s, release when the screen changes

mistakes.symptom: Back in Standard; all values back to defaults (SEN AUTO, FF 100, FFS PEA, NDP 50, NFR/NIN OFF, INT 11, FEI 100, FOR/SPR/DPR 100)
mistakes.cause: Tuning button held too long: manual says 4 s + 6 s more; one caption reads like 6 s total
mistakes.fix: Switch to Advanced again, select 1 SET, re-enter values from the pitwall Setup sheet

mistakes.symptom: Wheel not recognised properly on PS5
mistakes.cause: Base not in DARK BLUE mode (e.g. purple after experimenting, or mode changed after a firmware update)
mistakes.fix: Tap the power button until the ring is dark blue

mistakes.symptom: Base switched off while changing mode
mistakes.cause: Power button held 3 s instead of tapped
mistakes.fix: Power on again; slots are stored in the base

mistakes.symptom: In-game wheel turns more or less than the real wheel in F1 25
mistakes.cause: SEN differs from Maximum Wheel Rotation, or SEN AUTO
mistakes.fix: Set SEN by hand equal to Maximum Wheel Rotation; 90 deg check

mistakes.symptom: 'CAL' flashing or wheel off-centre after firmware update
Wheel does not return to centre
Brake/throttle don't reach 100% or show input at rest (stock CSL)
mistakes.fix: Press each pedal fully and release after every power-on

mistakes.cause: Stock CSL Pedals (no BRF) or load cell not detected

mistakes.symptom: Load-cell brake shows input with foot off
mistakes.fix: Firmware update and pedal reset on a PC

mistakes.symptom: FFS missing after fitting the Boost Kit
mistakes.fix: Nothing to fix. If FFS is still shown, set PEA (H-6NM, 2026-09-24)

mistakes.symptom: F1 25: violent oscillation or lost FFB after a session change
mistakes.fix: Pause and power-cycle the base; do not retune for it

mistakes.symptom: Switched to Advanced, more items appear, but values still won't change
Pressing the Tuning button shows nothing on the screen
mistakes.cause: Bent quick-release pins, or faulty wheel/base
mistakes.fix: Check the pins inside the quick release; try another wheel; contact Fanatec

mistakes.symptom: Menu opens on a number, not a profile name
mistakes.cause: Menu did not open on the profile item
mistakes.fix: Tilt LEFT or RIGHT until AUTO / C SET / SET n appears

mistakes.symptom: GT7: FFB lost and the wheel spins on its own
mistakes.cause: Known GT DD Pro issue in GT7 (App 1.6.1.3 notes)
mistakes.fix: Hands off; hold power 3 s to switch the base off; power on again
